title: The Leclanché Sealed Vacuum Galvanometer
alt: Brass and hand-blown glass vacuum galvanometer on mahogany base
description: Used in the basement laboratories of the Sorbonne to measure micro-currents during early electrolysis experiments. The hand-blown glass vacuum sphere prevented atmospheric oxidation of the gossamer silver thread.
provenance: Sorbonne Physical Laboratory Collection, Paris; acquired 1928.

title: Manuscript Folio 44: The Distillation of Antimony
alt: Aged parchment page with alchemical marginalia and furnace sketches
description: A clandestine recipe written in ciphered Latin by Bohemian metallurgical alchemists detailing the purification of stibnite into 'philosophical lead'. Note the charcoal burns along the lower perimeter.
provenance: Private Archive of the House of Rosenberg, Prague.

title: Culpeper-Type Brass Compound Microscope
alt: Three-pillar brass Culpeper microscope with wooden optical tube
description: Constructed with three brass scrolled legs mounted on a turned mahogany box base containing objective lenses. Used by amateur botanists to study crystalline structures of plant saps.
provenance: Royal Society of Edinburgh Historical Deposit.

title: The Cyanide Extraction Specimen Flask
alt: Heavy borosilicate glass laboratory beaker with ground stopper and amber residue
description: Recovered intact from the Glasgow metallurgical assay office. The amber tint was formulated to protect photosensitive cyanide compounds during gold leaching trials.

title: Glass Plate Negative: Spectral Lines of Sirius
alt: High-contrast photographic glass plate showing dark Fraunhofer absorption bands
description: Exposed over four hours on an unheated mountaintop in the Swiss Alps. The minute handwritten pencil notes identify previously uncataloged hydrogen Balmer transitions.
provenance: Jungfraujoch High Altitude Research Station Archive.

title: Dr. Vane's Field Herbarium Sheet (Solanaceae)
alt: Pressed botanical specimen mounted with gummed linen strips and inked notes
description: Gathered during the Upper Amazon drainage survey. Vane noted its paradoxical alkaloid potency, writing 'two drops numb the tongue for half a solar turn.'

title: The Woulfe Bottle Three-Neck Gas Receiver
alt: Thick green-tinted hand-blown triple-neck glass vessel
description: Revolutionary eighteenth-century apparatus designed to pass volatile gases through liquids without explosive pressure buildup. Critical to early pneumatic chemistry and oxygen isolation.

title: Silver-Plated Astronomical Sextant with Vernier Scale
alt: Intricate brass and silver navigational sextant with telescopic sight
description: Engraved by Troughton of London. Capable of reading lunar distances to within ten arcseconds, enabling precise calculation of longitude across ocean voyages.

title: Notebook of Anomalous Discharges (Vol. IV)
alt: Leather-bound notebook with grid pages and handwritten ink calculations
description: Contains sixty-four daily logs of unexplained fluorescent shadows cast upon barium platinocyanide screens when Crookes tubes were energized behind cardboard shields.

title: Geissler Low-Pressure Gas Discharge Tube
alt: Serpentine twisted glass tube filled with rarefied noble gases
description: Demonstrated the luminescent properties of electrified rarefied vapors. The hand-crafted spiral twists were designed to maximize optical path length for prism spectrographs.

title: The Chloroform Drop Dispenser Mask
alt: Wireframe respiratory mask covered in layered flannel gauze
description: Designed by Dr. John Snow for titrated vapor delivery. Transformed surgery from a barbaric race against shock into deliberate, measured physiological intervention.
provenance: St. Thomas's Hospital Surgical Museum, London.

title: Electrochemical Battery of Voltaic Discs
alt: Columnar pile of alternating zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked felt
description: The first source of continuous direct electric current in human history. Provided the spark that enabled Humphrey Davy to isolate sodium and potassium.

title: Lead-Shielded Radium Bromide Vial
alt: Heavy cylindrical cast-lead safe containing tiny glass capillary ampoule
description: Held 1.2 milligrams of purified radium salt. The interior of the box still exhibits faint phosphor luminescence due to residual gamma bombardment.

title: The Magdeburg Hemispheres Demonstration Set
alt: Pair of large polished copper hemispheres with iron ring handles
description: When fitted together and evacuated by an air pump, two teams of eight horses could not pull them apart, proving the crushing weight of atmospheric air.

title: Astronomical Astrolabe with Engraved Reticulated Rete
alt: Ornate brass planispheric astrolabe with gothic pointer fretwork
description: Calculated planetary positions, time of day from solar altitude, and astrological coordinates. Hand-engraved with latitude plates for Toledo, Cairo, and Nuremberg.
provenance: Nuremberg Guild of Metal Artisans Deposit.
